<a id="vsumm"></a>

## VSUMM: A mechanism designed to produce static video summaries and a novel evaluation method

- **Venue:** Pattern Recognition Letters 32(1), 56–68; online publication 2010
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://ic.unicamp.br/~sandra/pdf/papers/avila_PRL11.pdf)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/sandraavila/vsumm)
- **Encoders:** Handcrafted 16-bin HSV hue histograms; no pretrained neural encoder
- **Sampling:** One frame per second; remove near-monochromatic frames using feature variation
- **Architecture:** Cluster sampled frames; VSUMM1 uses all clusters; VSUMM2 retains clusters larger than half the average cluster size.
- **Fusion:** Visual-only histogram representation
- **Objective:** Section 3: per-video Euclidean k-means clustering with sequential initialization; no learned human-importance objective.
- **Training data:** No separate labelled training corpus
- **Test data:** 50 Open Video videos and 50 web videos in the original release
- **Split:** No supervised train/test split
- **Budget:** Variable keyframe count; no native 15% temporal budget
- **Postprocessing:** Choose centroid-nearest frames, remove similar keyframes and restore chronological order.
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/sandraavila/vsumm)
- **Code status:** Official data and CUS evaluation repository verified; complete summarizer source not independently verified
- **Framework:** CUS evaluator: Java with jai_core and jai_codec dependencies; summarizer framework Not reported
- **Weights:** Not applicable to handcrafted selector
- **Features:** Histogram features computed by the method; dataset release supplies media and user summaries.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper and official repository read; linked archives and Java evaluator were not downloaded or executed.
- **Limitations:** Static color-based matching can miss semantic equivalence. Extending selected frames into shots changes both the output and evaluation.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Authors:** Sandra Eliza Fontes de Avila; Ana Paula Brandão Lopes; Antonio da Luz Jr.; Arnaldo de Albuquerque Araújo
- **Year:** 2011
- **Supervision:** unsupervised
- **Tasks:** Generic static video summarization
- **Outputs:** Selected keyframe set
- **Mechanisms:** Color histograms; Modified k-means; Redundancy removal
- **Metrics:** CUS content matching; CUSA; CUSE
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://ic.unicamp.br/~sandra/pdf/papers/avila_PRL11.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/sandraavila/vsumm)

<a id="seqdpp"></a>

## Diverse Sequential Subset Selection for Supervised Video Summarization

- **Venue:** Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27 (NIPS 2014)
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~grauman/papers/nips14_seqdpp.pdf)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/pujols/Video-summarization)
- **Encoders:** 8192-D SIFT Fisher vectors, saliency and local context-correlation features
- **Sampling:** 1 fps, followed by candidate pruning
- **Architecture:** A conditional DPP selects within each temporal segment given the preceding selected subset; linear or tanh embeddings parameterize the kernel.
- **Fusion:** Handcrafted visual, saliency and context descriptors
- **Objective:** Maximum likelihood of oracle keyframe subsets under the sequential DPP factorization (Section 3, Eq. 8). Oracles are derived from human references.
- **Training data:** OVP, 39-video non-cartoon YouTube subset, and Kodak; dataset-specific training subsets
- **Test data:** OVP 50, YouTube 39, Kodak 18
- **Split:** 100 random 80/20 training/test trials per dataset
- **Budget:** Variable subset size; no universal 15% temporal budget
- **Postprocessing:** Approximate sequential MAP selection; no claim of exact global DPP MAP.
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/pujols/Video-summarization)
- **Code status:** Official MATLAB implementation and feature/oracle download advertised; source README inspected
- **Framework:** MATLAB; minFunc_2012 optimization; Java CUS evaluation dependencies
- **Weights:** Not independently verified
- **Features:** Author Dropbox package advertises Fisher features, saliency, context features, histograms, oracle and ground sets: https://www.dropbox.com/s/bpy41o2zglk4ka4/video_summarization.zip?dl=0
- **Reproducibility:** Primary paper and official seqDPP README read; Dropbox bytes, feature integrity and MATLAB execution not independently verified.
- **Limitations:** Local temporal conditioning does not enforce arbitrary long-range diversity. Human-reference oracle construction is part of training.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Authors:** Boqing Gong; Wei-Lun Chao; Kristen Grauman; Fei Sha
- **Year:** 2014
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** Generic static video summarization
- **Outputs:** Selected keyframe set
- **Mechanisms:** Sequential determinantal point process; Learned diversity kernel
- **Metrics:** Content-matched keyframe precision; Content-matched keyframe recall; Content-matched keyframe F1
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~grauman/papers/nips14_seqdpp.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/pujols/Video-summarization/blob/master/seqDPP/Readme_seqDPP.txt)

<a id="cosum"></a>

## Video Co-summarization: Video Summarization by Visual Co-occurrence

- **Venue:** CVPR 2015
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://people.csail.mit.edu/yalesong/publications/ChuSJ2015CVPR.pdf)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/l2ior/cosum)
- **Encoders:** CENTRIST, Dense-SIFT and HSV moments; concatenate and PCA-reduce to 400-D
- **Sampling:** Provided shot boundaries; exact frame sampling Not independently verified
- **Architecture:** Find mutually similar shot groups across topic-related videos using a bipartite graph.
- **Fusion:** Visual descriptors from multiple videos
- **Objective:** Section 3.4, Eq. 4: maximize weighted co-occurrence minus L1 sparsity penalties under pairwise similarity constraints; relaxed alternating updates.
- **Training data:** No human-summary training labels; joint optimization on the input video group
- **Test data:** CoSum: 51 video instances in ten groups; additional CMU-Mocap experiment
- **Split:** Collection-level unsupervised setting; no canonical training/test partition
- **Budget:** Evaluate top five and top fifteen shots
- **Postprocessing:** Rank shots by co-occurrence quality; select highest-ranked shots
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/l2ior/cosum)
- **Code status:** Official dataset/annotation and shot-index release; full algorithm implementation not independently verified
- **Framework:** Not independently verified
- **Weights:** Not independently verified
- **Features:** Paper describes handcrafted descriptors; ready-made tensor release not found in inspected repository
- **Reproducibility:** Paper and official data README inspected; video URLs were not downloaded.
- **Limitations:** Repeated visual content is a relevance proxy; source groups influence the summary. Input-group access must be recorded.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Authors:** Wen-Sheng Chu; Yale Song; Alejandro Jaimes
- **Year:** 2015
- **Supervision:** unsupervised
- **Tasks:** Multi-video co-summarization; Query-specific video summarization
- **Outputs:** Ranked shots per video
- **Mechanisms:** Cross-video visual co-occurrence; Maximal biclique finding; Sparse graph selection
- **Metrics:** mAP@5 shots; mAP@15 shots; Human concept-visualization ratings
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://people.csail.mit.edu/yalesong/publications/ChuSJ2015CVPR.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/l2ior/cosum)

<a id="submodular-mixtures"></a>

## Video Summarization by Learning Submodular Mixtures of Objectives

- **Venue:** CVPR 2015, 3090–3098
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://www.cv-foundation.org/openaccess/content_cvpr_2015/papers/Gygli_Video_Summarization_by_2015_CVPR_paper.pdf)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2015/html/Gygli_Video_Summarization_by_2015_CVPR_paper.html)
- **Encoders:** DeCAF visual descriptors and dataset-specific learned interestingness scores
- **Sampling:** UTE: 5-second segments; SumMe: superframes. Frame-sampling rate Not reported.
- **Architecture:** Nonnegative mixture of interestingness, representativeness and temporal-uniformity set functions.
- **Fusion:** Segment-level visual descriptors and interestingness
- **Objective:** Regularized large-margin learning of nonnegative mixture weights; projected subgradient optimization (Section 3, Eqs. 3–5).
- **Training data:** Annotated SumMe and UTE/VideoSET-derived references
- **Test data:** SumMe 25 and four UTE videos
- **Split:** Cross-testing; paper describes 100 randomized training/inference repetitions. Exact reusable split IDs Not reported.
- **Budget:** UTE: approximately 80 or 120 seconds. SumMe cap Not independently verified.
- **Postprocessing:** Compare lazy greedy selection by raw marginal gain and by gain/cost; return the better feasible set (Algorithm 1).
- **Code url:** Not independently verified
- **Code status:** No official implementation repository verified
- **Framework:** Not reported
- **Weights:** Not independently verified
- **Features:** Mean visual descriptors per candidate segment; downloadable tensors Not independently verified
- **Reproducibility:** Primary paper inspected; no code execution or score reproduction.
- **Limitations:** Learning uses labelled references. Budgeted greedy inference is approximate; text-based evaluation does not directly measure visual quality.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Authors:** Michael Gygli; Helmut Grabner; Luc Van Gool
- **Year:** 2015
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** Generic extractive video summarization
- **Outputs:** Selected temporal segments
- **Mechanisms:** Submodular mixtures; Large-margin learning; Budgeted greedy inference
- **Metrics:** Nearest-reference temporal F1 on SumMe; Text-mapped ROUGE on UTE
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://www.cv-foundation.org/openaccess/content_cvpr_2015/papers/Gygli_Video_Summarization_by_2015_CVPR_paper.pdf)

<a id="lstm-dpp"></a>

## Video Summarization with Long Short-term Memory

- **Venue:** ECCV 2016
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~grauman/papers/zhang-eccv2016-lstm-summ.pdf)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/kezhang-cs/Video-Summarization-with-LSTM)
- **Encoders:** ImageNet-pretrained GoogLeNet pool5, 1024-D
- **Sampling:** 2 fps
- **Architecture:** Bidirectional LSTM plus input-feature/hidden-state MLP predicts importance; dppLSTM adds a learned similarity embedding.
- **Fusion:** Concatenation of visual features and bidirectional recurrent states
- **Objective:** vsLSTM: squared-error importance regression. dppLSTM: regression pretraining followed by DPP maximum likelihood with quality-diversity kernel L_ij = y_i y_j phi_i^T phi_j (Section 3).
- **Training data:** Canonical: target 80% train/validation; augmented: add the other benchmark, OVP 50 and YouTube 39; transfer: other three datasets only.
- **Test data:** SumMe and TVSum
- **Split:** Random 80/20 canonical splits; augmentation/transfer as Table 3. Supplement Section 5.2: five runs per setting and test fold.
- **Budget:** 15% machine-summary duration; released TVSum reference evaluator uses 18%
- **Postprocessing:** KTS segments and budgeted keyshot decoding. The described DPP keyframe-density route differs from released diagonal-score reweighting followed by mean-shot knapsack.
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/kezhang-cs/Video-Summarization-with-LSTM)
- **Code status:** Official source pinned at 0ee0a0948872544567ecede76868287042470f75; no reproduction
- **Framework:** Python 2.7+, Theano 0.7+, MATLAB
- **Weights:** SumMe and TVSum trained model files listed in official tree; binaries not loaded
- **Features:** Advertised 2-fps GoogLeNet HDF5; original idx/fea_i schema. README data-download anchor lacks a file URL.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper, supplement and pinned evaluation source read; no model training, inference or archive integrity check.
- **Limitations:** Small benchmarks; fold hashes unavailable in paper. TVSum reference budget and dppLSTM decoder need explicit versioning for fair comparison.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Authors:** Ke Zhang; Wei-Lun Chao; Fei Sha; Kristen Grauman
- **Year:** 2016
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** Generic extractive video summarization
- **Outputs:** Frame importance scores; Selected keyshots
- **Mechanisms:** Bidirectional LSTM; Determinantal point process
- **Metrics:** Temporal-overlap F1; SumMe maximum across users; Temporal-overlap F1; TVSum mean across users

<a id="online-diversity-sampling"></a>

## Diversity Promoting Online Sampling for Streaming Video Summarization

- **Authors:** Rushil Anirudh; Ahnaf Masroor; Pavan Turaga
- **Venue:** ICIP
- **Year:** 2016
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICIP.2016.7532976)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://www.rushila.com/publications.html)
- **Supervision:** unsupervised; training-free
- **Tasks:** causal streaming video summarization; online keyframe selection
- **Outputs:** online keyframe set
- **Mechanisms:** online exemplar replacement; diversity maximization; convex-hull volume
- **Encoders:** ImageNet-pretrained VGG penultimate-layer features extracted with MatConvNet.
- **Sampling:** Single causal pass over VSUMM video frames; the experiment replaces the final 500 frames of every video with a frozen frame.
- **Architecture:** A generalization of online K-means maintains K exemplars using competitive replacement with Euclidean clustering cost and reduced-space convex-hull diversity. Online K-medoids is evaluated separately as a baseline; the proposed method also forces noisy updates on 1–10% of samples to escape local minima.
- **Fusion:** Visual-only streaming features; no cross-modal fusion.
- **Objective:** Training-free online clustering/diversity objective with O(K) memory and O(NK) analytical time.
- **Training data:** None beyond pretrained VGG.
- **Test data:** VSUMM: 50 MPEG-1 videos with five human keyframe summaries each, modified by frozen-frame suffixes for this experiment.
- **Split:** No learned split; all modified VSUMM videos are evaluated. K is chosen from each video's longest human reference summary, with K doubled when below five.
- **Budget:** User-specified K, but the reported experiment derives K from human reference sizes; this leaks reference budget information.
- **Postprocessing:** Fixed gamma 70 removes redundant exemplars before matching; evaluation then normalizes the number of matches by each user's reference-summary length.
- **Metrics:** user-wise normalized keyframe match
- **Code url:** Not independently verified
- **Code status:** No official or author-affiliated implementation found through exact-title, author-site and repository searches.
- **Framework:** Paper reports MATLAB/MatConvNet and an Intel i7 throughput experiment; no environment or source release.
- **Weights:** Pretrained VGG; no task checkpoint.
- **Features:** Online VGG frame embeddings; no released feature archive.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary paper and author publication page inspected; source, exact altered videos and evaluator were unavailable for execution.
- **Limitations:** The protocol alters every video, derives K from reference summaries and uses a modified VSUMM match metric rather than original precision/recall/F-score. No runs or uncertainty are reported. Throughput is hardware/implementation-specific and was not reproduced.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.09582) · [source 2](https://www.rushila.com/publications.html)

- **Weights:** Not independently verified

<a id="clip-it"></a>

## CLIP-It! Language-Guided Video Summarization

- **Authors:** Medhini Narasimhan; Anna Rohrbach; Trevor Darrell
- **Venue:** NeurIPS
- **Year:** 2021
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/7503cfacd12053d309b6bed5c89de212-Abstract.html)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://medhini.github.io/clip_it/)
- **Supervision:** supervised; unsupervised
- **Tasks:** generic extractive video summarization; natural-language query-focused video summarization; long-form egocentric summarization
- **Outputs:** frame importance; keyshot skim
- **Mechanisms:** vision-language pretraining; language-guided attention; caption-conditioned frame scoring
- **Encoders:** Fixed pretrained CLIP image/text encoders and off-the-shelf BMT captions; a Transformer with language-guided multi-head attention scores frames.
- **Sampling:** BMT consumes 2-fps frames, uniformly retaining seven captions for SumMe/TVSum and 15 for QFVS; Transformer sequences are limited to 256 steps.
- **Architecture:** CLIP text/image embeddings condition a frame-scoring Transformer; generic mode uses generated captions and query mode uses free-form text.
- **Fusion:** Language-guided attention aligns CLIP visual and text features before temporal scoring.
- **Objective:** Supervised weighted binary cross-entropy plus diversity and reconstruction losses; the paper's unsupervised variant drops BCE but still uses pretrained CLIP and BMT.
- **Training data:** SumMe and TVSum; 39 YouTube and 50 OVP videos in augmented/transfer protocols; QFVS/UT Egocentric for query-focused evaluation.
- **Test data:** SumMe, TVSum and QFVS under separate generic, augmented, transfer, generated-caption and query-focused settings.
- **Split:** TVSum uses five random 20% test splits; SumMe refers to available splits without identifying hashes. QFVS uses four leave-one-video-out rounds with one validation and two training videos.
- **Budget:** QFVS uses fixed 5-second shots. The paper delegates generic frame-to-keyshot conversion to prior code and does not restate segmentation, duration budget or reference aggregation.
- **Postprocessing:** Frame scores are averaged into shots and selected by 0/1 knapsack; oracle ground-truth-caption experiments are isolated from generated-caption results.
- **Metrics:** keyshot F-score; Kendall tau; Spearman rho; QFVS concept F-score
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/medhini/clip_it)
- **Code status:** Official author repository is a README-only stub stating that code is coming; an incomplete unofficial forward-pass reimplementation is indexed separately.
- **Framework:** Paper reports Adam, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 0.001, 20 epochs, batch size 100 and five RTX 2080 GPUs; no official runnable environment.
- **Weights:** Fixed CLIP and BMT models; no official task checkpoint released.
- **Features:** CLIP/BMT features and captions are not released through executable author code.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper, project page, official stub commit c18180905fa5a56c2297f89ae4c5ccae8d05f180 and unofficial source were inspected; no model or archive was run.
- **Limitations:** The unsupervised label applies only to loss design, not pretrained components. Generic summary construction and SumMe split identity are underspecified. Ground-truth-caption oracle rows are not deployable. Official code is unavailable and the unofficial repository omits training, data, losses, evaluation and decoding.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/7503cfacd12053d309b6bed5c89de212-Paper.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/medhini/clip_it/tree/c18180905fa5a56c2297f89ae4c5ccae8d05f180) · [source 3](https://github.com/srpkdyy/CLIP-It/tree/afb5ef27d77fe4ebf95960fdb63a46bc40832a82)

- **Authors:** Bo He; Jun Wang; Jielin Qiu; Trung Bui; Abhinav Shrivastava; Zhaowen Wang
- **Venue:** CVPR
- **Year:** 2023
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.07284)

- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** multimodal summarization; generic video summarization; livestream summarization

- **Sampling:** Time-stamped video frames and transcript sentences; dataset-dependent sampling.
- **Architecture:** Multimodal Transformer, modality experts and two importance heads.
- **Fusion:** Shared segment positional embeddings and alignment-guided self-attention exploit transcript/frame timing.
- **Objective:** Section 3.4: modality focal classification losses plus inter-sample and intra-sample contrastive terms. Intra-sample positives use ground-truth summaries.

- **Test data:** SumMe; TVSum; Daily Mail; CNN; BLiSS.
- **Split:** Dataset-specific splits and standard-video splits in Appendix B; exact split artifacts not independently verified.
- **Budget:** Dataset-dependent; exact configuration not independently verified.
- **Postprocessing:** Dataset-dependent visual/text subset selection.
- **Metrics:** F1; Kendall tau; Spearman rho; ROUGE-1; ROUGE-2; ROUGE-L; cosine image similarity

- **Weights:** Official README links checkpoint archive on Google Drive; archive contents not downloaded.
- **Features:** Author feature archive; BLiSS raw-video URLs require contacting authors per README.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary-source and official repository at commit 5c7dceac3e81aca297e28c987f472ac3b9a9dbb6 inspected; no model was executed.
- **Limitations:** Contrastive losses do not make this label-free: classification and within-example contrast require annotated summaries. BLiSS livestream source does not establish causal online processing.

<a id="csum"></a>

## Learning to Summarize Videos by Contrasting Clips

- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (v3)
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05213)
- **Project url:** Not reported
- **Encoders:** Evaluates existing backbones unchanged: vsLSTM, dppLSTM, VASNet, MSVA (GoogLeNet/multi-source visual features) for summarization, and UMT (visual + optional audio) for YouTube Highlights.
- **Sampling:** Standard benchmark clip/frame feature sequences from MSVA (SumMe/TVSum) and UMT (YouTube Highlights); sub-video window length n=10 clips in contrastive distance.
- **Architecture:** Backbone score predictor paired with a differentiable top-k frame/clip selector (Successive Halving default; Sinkhorn and Perturbed top-k ablated) and projection head h.
- **Fusion:** Visual-only for vsLSTM/dppLSTM/VASNet; multi-source visual fusion for MSVA; visual or audio-visual fusion for UMT on YouTube Highlights.
- **Objective:** Unsupervised clip-contrastive InfoNCE loss (Eq. 1) using sub-video distribution distance dist_n (Eq. 4, n=10) over differentiable top-k selected clips; optional 50-epoch supervised fine-tuning on YouTube Highlights.
- **Training data:** SumMe, TVSum, and YouTube Highlights training folds (20-epoch unsupervised contrastive pretraining; optional 50-epoch supervised fine-tuning on YouTube Highlights).
- **Test data:** TVSum; SumMe; YouTube Highlights
- **Split:** 5-fold cross-validation using the same splits as MSVA on SumMe and TVSum; standard YouTube Highlights splits.
- **Budget:** Top-k frame selection during training/inference for summarization; score threshold Theta tuned on a holdout set for YouTube Highlights.
- **Postprocessing:** Selects top-N highest-scored frames for summarization; applies Gaussian smoothing and threshold Theta for highlight detection.
- **Code url:** Not reported in paper; no official repository found
- **Code status:** No official or author-affiliated repository found via title and author searches
- **Framework:** Not reported in primary paper
- **Weights:** Not released
- **Features:** Standard SumMe, TVSum (MSVA), and YouTube Highlights (UMT) pre-extracted feature sets.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary arXiv v3 paper inspected in full; no code or checkpoints released.
- **Limitations:** Optional personal labels must not be mixed into unsupervised comparison. Few-shot tag refers to the labeled personalization framing in the introduction, whereas experiments evaluate unsupervised contrastive training and supervised highlight fine-tuning. Exact KTS/knapsack postprocessing details on SumMe/TVSum are delegated to baseline pipelines.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Authors:** Ivan Sosnovik; Artem Moskalev; Cees Kaandorp; Arnold Smeulders
- **Supervision:** unsupervised; self-supervised; few-shot
- **Tasks:** generic single-video; personalized
- **Outputs:** keyshot/video skim
- **Mechanisms:** contrastive learning; differentiable top-k
- **Metrics:** temporal F1; Kendall tau; Spearman rho; mAP
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05213) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.05213v3)
- **Year:** 2023

<a id="multi-vidsum"></a>

## A Challenging Multimodal Video Summary: Simultaneously Extracting and Generating Keyframe-Caption Pairs from Video

- **Authors:** Keito Kudo; Haruki Nagasawa; Jun Suzuki; Nobuyuki Shimizu
- **Venue:** EMNLP
- **Year:** 2023
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.457/)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/cl-tohoku/Multi-VidSum)
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** multimodal video summarization; joint keyframe-caption generation
- **Outputs:** ordered keyframes; aligned captions
- **Mechanisms:** iterative segmentation and refinement; joint pointer-caption decoding; dynamic-programming alignment
- **Encoders:** CLIP frame features; iterative captioners include Vid2Seq/InstructBLIP, while the simultaneous model uses a Flan-T5-base encoder-decoder with gate and pointer.
- **Sampling:** Frames are sampled every 0.5 seconds. Joint experiment configurations use maximum input length 2,048 and beam width eight.
- **Architecture:** One baseline iteratively segments, captions, refines keyframes and uses dynamic programming; another jointly decodes captions and frame pointers.
- **Fusion:** Visual frame tokens and language tokens share the joint encoder-decoder; iterative variants score generated captions against temporal candidates.
- **Objective:** Equal-weight keyframe-pointer and caption cross-entropies; pseudo-pretraining on MS COCO then Visual Storytelling precedes Multi-VidSum fine-tuning.
- **Training data:** 7,727 Multi-VidSum/ActivityNet training videos, with MS COCO and Visual Storytelling pseudo-pretraining for the joint model.
- **Test data:** 439 re-captioned videos sampled from ActivityNet Captions' original validation partition.
- **Split:** Original ActivityNet test references are unavailable. The 439-video evaluation subset is drawn from 4,282 validation videos; experiment validation subsets are randomly sampled and no shared split hash is reported in the paper.
- **Budget:** A predefined N pairs; released joint configurations use N=4. Iterative dynamic programming minimizes temporal overlap across selected pairs.
- **Postprocessing:** Iterative mode combines 20 MTM and PySceneDetect segments, drops segments longer than 75% of the video, refines four times and chooses N pairs by dynamic programming; joint mode uses beam search.
- **Metrics:** AKM exact; AKM cosine; BLEURT; METEOR
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/cl-tohoku/Multi-VidSum)
- **Code status:** Official training/preparation and separate evaluator repositories inspected at pinned commits; no runtime reproduction performed.
- **Framework:** Docker, PyTorch/Hugging Face, Weights & Biases and four GPUs; exact dependencies are repository-configured and large downloads are external.
- **Weights:** Pretrained CLIP, Flan-T5, Vid2Seq/InstructBLIP variants; no locally verified checkpoint bundle.
- **Features:** CLIP frame features, captions and candidate-frame annotations; the official dataset listing was pinned at ca03b147ddb4959229b510bde8eacc55933088af, but its 33.8 GB archive was not downloaded.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper, source commit 23a053970824926c2ae421ab9d5956ce133348b7, evaluator commit d4aa2fd4f1b88b65a14f2c66676fe1529572772a and dataset listing ca03b147ddb4959229b510bde8eacc55933088af were inspected; source was not executed and the archive was not downloaded.
- **Limitations:** Keyframe and caption metrics require constrained reference alignment and are not comparable with keyshot F1. The evaluation set repurposes validation data. The dataset card declares Apache-2.0, but source/evaluator repositories have no standard license; InstructBLIP zero/few-shot captioning does not make the complete summarizer zero/few-shot.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.457.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/cl-tohoku/Multi-VidSum/tree/23a053970824926c2ae421ab9d5956ce133348b7) · [source 3](https://github.com/cl-tohoku/Multi-VidSum-Eval/tree/d4aa2fd4f1b88b65a14f2c66676fe1529572772a) · [source 4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/tohoku-nlp/multi-vidsum/tree/ca03b147ddb4959229b510bde8eacc55933088af)

<a id="personalized-daylong-egocentric"></a>

## Generating Personalized Summaries of Day Long Egocentric Videos

- **Authors:** Pravin Nagar; Anuj Rathore; C. V. Jawahar; Chetan Arora
- **Venue:** IEEE TPAMI (online 2021; archival volume 2023)
- **Year:** 2023
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2021.3118077)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://pravin74.github.io/Int-sum/index.html)
- **Supervision:** unsupervised
- **Tasks:** personalized egocentric video summarization; day-long video summarization; interactive variable-length summarization
- **Outputs:** keyframe sub-shot skim; variable-length summary
- **Mechanisms:** policy gradient; actor-critic; user-feedback rewards
- **Encoders:** 512-dimensional C3D pool-5 features pretrained on Sports-1M feed a bidirectional LSTM policy over non-overlapping 16-frame sub-shots.
- **Sampling:** Non-overlapping 16-frame sub-shots; sliding windows span 25% of the desired summary length and four full-video passes process day-long streams.
- **Architecture:** Binary selection policy trained with policy-gradient, Q-learning or actor-critic; reward plug-ins encode distinctiveness, indicativeness, target length, faces/social interactions/identities and positive/negative user examples.
- **Fusion:** Visual policy rewards are augmented with face, identity, interaction and user-example signals rather than a learned multimodal fusion block.
- **Objective:** Unsupervised RL rewards for distinctiveness, indicativeness and requested length, optionally extended by explicit personalization feedback.
- **Training data:** Disney day-long egocentric videos, UTE, HUJI and ancillary SumMe/TVSum experiments; pretrained feature/detector models supply representations.
- **Test data:** Disney, UTE and HUJI long-form corpora; SumMe and TVSum under fixed DR-DSN splits.
- **Split:** Disney has eight sequences but reference summaries for only three videos with three annotators; UTE has four videos. SumMe/TVSum use five fixed DR-DSN splits; exact files were not rehashed.
- **Budget:** Variable requested lengths for day-long output; a fixed five-minute summary for reported Disney/UTE RFS-50 comparison; 15% duration for SumMe/TVSum.
- **Postprocessing:** Four-pass sliding-window decisions are assembled into a skim; optional GUI feedback changes rewards for subsequent personalized summaries.
- **Metrics:** RFS-50; BLEU; average human rating; unique events minus jerks; traditional 15%-duration F-score over 16-frame sub-shot selections
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/Pravin74/interact_summ_code)
- **Code status:** Official author source inspected at a pinned commit; GUI/script workflow is incomplete without separately acquired feature files.
- **Framework:** README reports Ubuntu 16.04/18.04, PyTorch 1.4, CUDA 9/10.1 and NVIDIA P5000; no dependency lock.
- **Weights:** Pretrained C3D, Faster R-CNN and OpenFace dependencies; no end-to-end checkpoint package verified.
- **Features:** Users must acquire and rename C3D HDF5 features; acquisition and integrity are not automated.
- **Reproducibility:** Accepted manuscript, project page and source commit b18da63203581c532eb4ad50ad7837fee3f300e6 were inspected; models and data were not executed/downloaded.
- **Limitations:** Only three day-long Disney videos have reference summaries and the personalization study has ten users. RFS-50 depends on a temporal tolerance and is not ordinary F1. The project-page BLEU claim conflicts in scale with manuscript Table 2. No license or locked environment is provided.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://www.cse.iitd.ac.in/~chetan/papers/pravin-pami21.pdf) · [source 2](https://pravin74.github.io/Int-sum/index.html) · [source 3](https://github.com/Pravin74/interact_summ_code/tree/b18da63203581c532eb4ad50ad7837fee3f300e6)

<a id="self-vs"></a>

## SELF-VS: Self-supervised Encoding Learning For Video Summarization

- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15993)
- **Project url:** Not reported
- **Encoders:** Teacher: Kinetics-pretrained 3D CNN (R3D-18) last-layer video representation; Student: ImageNet-pretrained GoogLeNet pool5 (1024-D) frame features with positional encoding.
- **Sampling:** 2 fps uniform downsampling for both UCF101 pretraining and SumMe/TVSum fine-tuning.
- **Architecture:** Two serial 6-layer Transformer encoders (4 heads, d_model=256, d_head=64, dropout=0.2) with a linear+softmax frame-weighting head that constructs a score-weighted video representation.
- **Fusion:** Visual-only; frame features are weighted by predicted softmax importance scores W = softmax(X W_s) to form a student video embedding matched to the frozen R3D-18 teacher.
- **Objective:** Stage 1 (SSL pretraining): cross-entropy knowledge distillation loss between softmaxed R3D-18 teacher and score-weighted Transformer student distributions (30 epochs, batch size 512, Adam lr=1e-4). Stage 2 (fine-tuning): supervised MSE against ground-truth frame importance scores (25 epochs, batch size 4, Adam lr=1e-3).
- **Training data:** UCF101 (~13k videos, 2–10s) for self-supervised pretraining; SumMe and TVSum training splits for supervised fine-tuning.
- **Test data:** SumMe; TVSum
- **Split:** Five splits from Zhang et al. (2016) on SumMe and TVSum.
- **Budget:** 15% summary budget for F-score evaluation; full frame-score ranking for Kendall tau and Spearman rho.
- **Postprocessing:** Both F-score and rank correlations (tau, rho) are averaged across multiple user annotations; paper notes poor F-score (39.80 SumMe, 58.99 TVSum) due to relative-score pretraining and KTS sensitivity, while achieving tau=0.176, rho=0.232 on TVSum.
- **Code url:** Not reported in paper; no official repository found
- **Code status:** No official or author-affiliated repository found via title and author searches
- **Framework:** PyTorch 1.12.1 on Arch Linux (RTX 3060, Intel Core i5, 16 GB RAM)
- **Weights:** Uses pretrained R3D-18 (Kinetics) and GoogLeNet (ImageNet); no SELF-VS checkpoints released.
- **Features:** GoogLeNet pool5 frame features and R3D-18 clip features at 2 fps; not publicly archived by authors.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary arXiv v1 paper inspected in full (including PyTorch-style pseudocode in Algorithm 1); no public repository or checkpoints found.
- **Limitations:** Pretraining relies on a supervised Kinetics-pretrained R3D-18 action recognition teacher, and downstream evaluation still requires 25 epochs of supervised MSE fine-tuning on ground-truth frame scores. F-score lags behind baselines (39.80 on SumMe) because softmax pretraining weights do not calibrate absolute score magnitudes.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Authors:** Hojjat Mokhtarabadi; Kave Bahraman; Mehrdad HosseinZadeh; Mahdi Eftekhari
- **Supervision:** self-supervised; supervised
- **Tasks:** generic single-video
- **Outputs:** keyshot/video skim
- **Mechanisms:** knowledge distillation; transformer
- **Metrics:** temporal F1; Kendall tau; Spearman rho
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15993) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.15993v1)
- **Year:** 2023

## Progressive Video Summarization via Multimodal Self-supervised Learning

- **Authors:** Haopeng Li; Qiuhong Ke; Mingming Gong; Tom Drummond
- **Venue:** WACV
- **Year:** 2023
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2023/html/Li_Progressive_Video_Summarization_via_Multimodal_Self-Supervised_Learning_WACV_2023_paper.html)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/HopLee6/SSPVS-PyTorch)
- **Supervision:** self-supervised; supervised
- **Tasks:** generic extractive video summarization; text-assisted video summarization
- **Outputs:** frame importance; keyshot skim
- **Mechanisms:** multimodal self-supervised pretraining; progressive frame reweighting; optional text conditioning
- **Encoders:** ImageNet-pretrained GoogLeNet pool-5 frame features, a Transformer video encoder and uncased BERT-base text encoder.
- **Sampling:** YTVT, SumMe and TVSum are sampled at 2 fps. Pretraining randomly crops 256 frames; downstream training randomly crops or zero-pads to 512 frames.
- **Architecture:** Video-text pretraining combines coarse correspondence, fine-grained set alignment and masked-frame recovery; a one-to-four-stage progressive summarizer repeatedly reweights frame features.
- **Fusion:** Optional category/query/title text is encoded by BERT and fused into the first progressive stage.
- **Objective:** Three self-supervised pretraining losses followed by supervised mean-squared error against human frame-importance scores.
- **Training data:** YTVT (3,081 videos, 23 categories and 202 queries) for self-supervised pretraining; SumMe/TVSum human scores for fine-tuning; OVP and YouTube in augmented/transfer protocols.
- **Test data:** SumMe and TVSum under five-fold canonical, augmented and transfer settings.
- **Split:** Five-fold cross-validation is reported, but the paper does not identify split hashes. Released source uses each fold's test_keys for validation and post-hoc best-epoch selection.
- **Budget:** KTS shots selected by 0/1 knapsack under a strict 15% video-length constraint.
- **Postprocessing:** Mean frame importance per KTS shot becomes the knapsack value; SumMe uses average-reference and TVSum max-reference F-score aggregation in released code.
- **Metrics:** Kendall tau; Spearman rho; keyshot F-score
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/HopLee6/SSPVS-PyTorch)
- **Code status:** Official author repository inspected at a pinned commit; no runtime reproduction performed.
- **Framework:** Python 3.8.13, PyTorch 1.12, PyTorch Lightning 1.6.5, OR-Tools 9.3.10497 and pytorch-transformers 1.2.0.
- **Weights:** README links Figshare checkpoints; files were not downloaded or loaded.
- **Features:** README links processed data, frame features and text metadata on Figshare; archive bodies and hashes were not inspected.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper and source at commit e472200069b1697e392f7ac278593c973026b680 were inspected; no model, checkpoint or dataset archive was executed or downloaded.
- **Limitations:** Self-supervision applies to representation pretraining, not the final summarizer, which uses human importance labels. Released source selects the best epoch using test_keys after training, creating test-influenced model selection. The repository has no standard license and restricts use to non-commercial research/education.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2023/papers/Li_Progressive_Video_Summarization_via_Multimodal_Self-Supervised_Learning_WACV_2023_paper.pdf) · [source 2](https://github.com/HopLee6/SSPVS-PyTorch/tree/e472200069b1697e392f7ac278593c973026b680)

<a id="csta"></a>

## CSTA: CNN-based Spatiotemporal Attention for Video Summarization

- **Venue:** CVPR
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11905)
- **Project url:** Not reported
- **Encoders:** Frozen ImageNet-pretrained GoogLeNet pool5 (1024-D) frame features replicated to 3 channels with a learnable 3x1024 CLS token; MobileNet-V2, EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 evaluated in ablations.
- **Sampling:** 2-fps subsampled frame features; on TVSum, subsampled frame scores are expanded to full frames via nearest-pick assignment.
- **Architecture:** Trainable 2D GoogLeNet CNN over 3-channel stacked frame-feature matrices, adaptive average pooling, skip connection, time/dimension softmax Mixing Module, and 2-layer MLP classifier.
- **Fusion:** Visual-only; temporal attention (Att_T) and spatial/dimension attention (Att_D) are combined via element-wise multiplication with value embeddings and summed.
- **Objective:** Supervised mean squared error (MSE) between predicted frame scores and averaged ground-truth annotations; Adam (lr=1e-3, weight decay=1e-7, dropout=0.6, batch size=1, 100 epochs).
- **Training data:** SumMe; TVSum (80% training folds under non-overlapping 5-fold cross-validation).
- **Test data:** SumMe; TVSum
- **Split:** Non-overlapping 5-fold cross-validation (80% train / 20% test) repeated 10 times; best epoch per split selected on test rank correlation (Appendix A.1).
- **Budget:** 15% summary duration budget via KTS shot segmentation and 0/1 knapsack selection.
- **Postprocessing:** SumMe evaluates Kendall tau and Spearman rho between binary 0/1 KTS+knapsack summary videos and human summary videos; TVSum evaluates tau and rho on 2-fps subsampled frame scores expanded to full frames against 20 user annotations (Appendix D and evaluation_metrics.py).
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/thswodnjs3/CSTA)
- **Code status:** Official repository inspected at commit b070f7d910b227e040dad66ec9f18b60dac5ea3d; linked by CVPR paper
- **Framework:** Python / PyTorch (repository requirements.txt specifies torch, numpy, h5py, scipy, ortools, tqdm; trained on RTX 4090)
- **Weights:** No pretrained CSTA checkpoint committed in repository; uses torchvision ImageNet-pretrained GoogLeNet weights.
- **Features:** Uses standard eccv16_dataset_summe_google_pool5.h5 and eccv16_dataset_tvsum_google_pool5.h5 HDF5 feature packages.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary CVPR paper, supplementary material and official repository at commit b070f7d910b227e040dad66ec9f18b60dac5ea3d inspected; no model execution.
- **Limitations:** Test-set correlation is used for best-epoch selection per split (Appendix A.1). SumMe correlations are computed on discretized binary summary masks whereas TVSum correlations are computed on frame-expanded continuous importance scores (Appendix D). Record evaluation-code revision: downsampled-only versus full-timeline summary generation changes the reported protocol.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Authors:** Jaewon Son; Jaehun Park; Kwangsu Kim
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** generic single-video
- **Outputs:** keyshot/video skim
- **Mechanisms:** convolution; attention
- **Metrics:** temporal F1; Kendall tau; Spearman rho
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11905) · [source 2](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Son_CSTA_CNN-based_Spatiotemporal_Attention_for_Video_Summarization_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf) · [source 3](https://github.com/thswodnjs3/CSTA/tree/b070f7d910b227e040dad66ec9f18b60dac5ea3d)
- **Year:** 2024

- **Venue:** CVPR

## VideoXum: Cross-modal Visual and Textural Summarization of Videos

- **Authors:** Jingyang Lin; Hang Hua; Ming Chen; Yikang Li; Jenhao Hsiao; Chiuman Ho; Jiebo Luo
- **Venue:** IEEE Transactions on Multimedia 26:5548-5560 (2024); accepted 2023
- **Year:** 2024
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12060)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://videoxum.github.io/)
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** video-to-video; video-to-text; joint visual-text summarization
- **Outputs:** selected frames; text summary
- **Mechanisms:** multitask supervised learning; vision-language encoder-decoder
- **Encoders:** BLIP visual encoder and pretrained text decoder; VTSUM-BLIP baseline.
- **Sampling:** 1 frame per second in VideoXum representation.
- **Architecture:** Shared video representation feeds frame-importance and text-generation decoders.
- **Fusion:** Shared visual encoding supports jointly aligned visual and text outputs.
- **Objective:** Section IV-B Eqs. (6)-(7): frame binary cross-entropy plus autoregressive text negative log likelihood; overall multitask objective Section IV-C.
- **Training data:** VideoXum human summary annotations derived from ActivityNet Captions.
- **Test data:** VideoXum.
- **Split:** 8,000 train / 2,001 validation / 4,000 test videos (Section III-A).
- **Budget:** Paper: intended top 15% of frames. Inspected F1 helper keeps scores >= the zero-based threshold at floor(0.15*N), selecting floor(0.15*N)+1 frames with distinct scores and possibly more with ties.
- **Postprocessing:** Frame threshold selection, not KTS keyshots. F1 is computed for each human mask and aggregated; the rank-metric path compares scores with the mean of ten masks. VT-CLIPScore uses a separate top-k path.
- **Metrics:** F1; Kendall tau; Spearman rho; BLEU; METEOR; ROUGE-L; CIDEr; VT-CLIPScore
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/jylins/videoxum)
- **Code status:** Official source inspected at commit 11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df; linked artifacts were not downloaded or run.
- **Framework:** PyTorch; repository documents Python 3.8 / PyTorch 1.10.1.
- **Weights:** Official model zoo on Hugging Face linked by repository.
- **Features:** Author-provided annotations and model/feature preparation instructions.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary paper and selected source inspected at commit 11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df; no model execution or independent result reproduction.
- **Limitations:** Repository badge uses TMM 2023; archival volume is 2024. Released F1 threshold can exceed the intended 15% frame budget. F1 reference averaging and correlation against the mean reference are distinct; neither is the classic KTS keyshot protocol.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-08
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.12060v3) · [source 2](https://videoxum.github.io/) · [source 3](https://github.com/jylins/videoxum/tree/11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df) · [source 4](https://github.com/jylins/videoxum/blob/11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df/utils.py#L255-L281) · [source 5](https://github.com/jylins/videoxum/blob/11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df/eval_v2vt_sum.py#L53-L107)

## QEVA: A Reference-Free Evaluation Metric for Narrative Video Summarization with Multimodal Question Answering

- **Authors:** Woojun Jung; Junyeong Kim
- **Venue:** Findings of EMNLP 2025 (pp. 24632–24642); arXiv mirror posted 2026-04-27
- **Year:** 2025
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1340/)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/jungnerd/QEVA)
- **Supervision:** training-free
- **Tasks:** reference-free evaluation of video-to-text summarization; narrative video summarization meta-evaluation
- **Outputs:** Coverage QA score; Factuality QA score; Chronology QA score; composite QEVA score
- **Mechanisms:** multimodal question generation and answering; two-stage trivial and low-quality QA filtering; three-dimensional narrative summary evaluation
- **Encoders:** Default setup uses Gemini-1.5-Pro as the Video-LMM and GPT-4o as the LLM; open-source ablations evaluate Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, LLaMA-3.1 and Gemma-3.
- **Sampling:** Full source videos from MLVU (~15 minutes average duration) fed to the Video-LMM for Coverage and Chronology question generation and Factuality verification.
- **Architecture:** Three-branch QA evaluation pipeline: (1) Video-LMM generates 10 high-level Coverage questions answered by an LLM from the candidate summary; (2) LLM extracts 10 categorical factual claims from the summary verified by a Video-LMM against the video; (3) Video-LMM segments events and generates 10 boolean/multiple-choice/ordering Chronology questions answered by an LLM from the summary.
- **Fusion:** Collaborative Video-LMM and text-LLM question-answering pipeline with cross-model triviality (no-context) and ambiguity (with-context) filtering.
- **Objective:** No task training; QEVA(S, V) is the arithmetic mean of filtered question-answering accuracy across Coverage, Factuality and Chronology on a [0, 1] scale.
- **Training data:** None; meta-evaluated on MLVU(VS)-Eval.
- **Test data:** MLVU(VS)-Eval: 200 videos from MLVU Video Summarization task with 800 candidate summaries generated by GPT-4o, InternVL3-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Video-LLaVA-7B, rated by 20 human annotators (two per summary, Krippendorff's alpha = 0.68).
- **Split:** 200-video evaluation benchmark (800 model summaries); no train/test split required for reference-free metric correlation.
- **Budget:** 10 generated QA pairs per dimension before two-stage filtering; no temporal skim budget.
- **Postprocessing:** Two-stage filtering removes questions answered correctly without context (trivial) or answered incorrectly even with full context (ambiguous/low-quality) before averaging.
- **Metrics:** Kendall tau_b; Kendall tau_c; Spearman rho; Krippendorff alpha
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/jungnerd/QEVA)
- **Code status:** Official repository inspected at commit 657cad6bff56e3cb25bf41610c020ce68787abd3; currently a placeholder README with no code or dataset files committed.
- **Framework:** Gemini-1.5-Pro and GPT-4o APIs (or Qwen2.5-VL/InternVL3 + LLaMA-3.1/Gemma-3); full prompt templates are provided in paper Appendix A.
- **Weights:** Proprietary API or off-the-shelf open-weight Video-LMM/LLM checkpoints.
- **Features:** LanguageBind used only for the Video-Summary Similarity baseline; QEVA operates on raw video and text summaries.
- **Reproducibility:** ACL Anthology / arXiv full text and official repository stub at commit 657cad6bff56e3cb25bf41610c020ce68787abd3 inspected; full prompt templates are published in the paper, but evaluation code and MLVU(VS)-Eval annotations are not yet uploaded to the GitHub repository.
- **Limitations:** Relies on multi-call Video-LMM and LLM inference, incurring API cost and potential LMM hallucinations or self-preference bias. Lower correlation is observed on short, low-quality Video-LLaVA summaries. The linked GitHub repository is still an empty stub.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1340/) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24052v1) · [source 3](https://github.com/jungnerd/QEVA/tree/657cad6bff56e3cb25bf41610c020ce68787abd3)

## AdaFrame: Hierarchical Multimodal Deduplication with Adaptive Information Budgeting for Cost-Efficient Video Advertisement Analysis

- **Authors:** Abdul Basit Tonmoy; Arman Luthra; Guang Lin; Qixin Deng
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19127v1)
- **Project url:** Not reported
- **Supervision:** training-free
- **Tasks:** adaptive keyframe selection and deduplication; cost-efficient VLM video advertisement analysis
- **Outputs:** deduplicated keyframe set with timestamps; structured 11-field JSON video ad metadata
- **Mechanisms:** three-tier deduplication cascade (pHash/dHash/wHash voting -> AlexNet LPIPS -> CLIP K-means); SVD-based Intrinsic Semantic Dimensionality (ISD) and Semantic Energy frame budgeting; Temporal-Aware Non-Maximum Suppression (TA-NMS)
- **Encoders:** CLIP ViT-B/32 (512-D) for semantic clustering and velocity; AlexNet LPIPS for perceptual similarity; Whisper-large-v3 for speech transcription; Tesseract 5.3 for OCR; Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude 3 Haiku for downstream VLM extraction.
- **Sampling:** PySceneDetect content-aware scene segmentation (threshold 27.0) followed by 50 ms chi-square histogram change detection (min 100 ms gap), reducing a 30s/30fps video from ~900 frames to ~150 candidates and 24.6 final selected frames on average.
- **Architecture:** Seven-stage parallel audio-visual pipeline: (1) ingestion, (2) PySceneDetect segmentation, (3) 50 ms histogram candidate extraction, (4) 3-tier deduplication (hash majority vote theta_h=10 removing 37.5%, LPIPS theta_l=0.15 removing 19.5%, CLIP K-means with K=k* removing 53.3%), (5) parallel VAD + Whisper-large-v3 + promo keyphrase + audio mood pipeline, (6) multimodal importance scoring + SVD ISD budget + TA-NMS (tau_nms=2.0s, lambda=0.3), and (7) single-pass VLM JSON extraction.
- **Fusion:** Candidate frame importance combines opening/closing positional boosts (1.4–1.5x), scene boundary proximity (1.2–1.4x), audio energy/keyphrase alignment (1.3–1.5x), and OCR text/face presence (1.2–1.3x), while audio transcripts and mood labels are appended to the VLM prompt.
- **Objective:** Training-free information-budgeted selection: k* = min{k : sum_{i=1}^k sigma_i^2 / sum_{j=1}^N sigma_j^2 >= 0.90} from SVD of centered CLIP embeddings caps the adaptive frame budget min(base + floor(1.5*k*), max(base, floor(base + d*rho*E_S))).
- **Training data:** No model training; attention-yield weights (alpha=0.4, beta=0.35, gamma=0.25) tuned via grid search on 50 held-out ads.
- **Test data:** 500 randomly sampled video advertisements from the Pitt Ads Dataset (3,477 total ads; 38 topic classes, 30 sentiment classes, 1–5 effectiveness scale).
- **Split:** 50 held-out ads for hyperparameter grid search; 500 randomly sampled Pitt Ads videos for main evaluation across 10 frame-selection methods (including DSNet, PySceneDetect, CLIP-Only, Uniform-1FPS, Gemini Native).
- **Budget:** Adaptive per-video frame budget governed by ISD k* and Semantic Energy E_S (realized mean 24.6 frames/video vs. 47.7 for Uniform-1FPS and 200.1 for DSNet; 48% frame reduction and 75% VLM cost reduction).
- **Postprocessing:** Temporal-Aware NMS (TA-NMS) selects 1 frame per K-means cluster with exponential temporal decay exp(-&#124;t_f - t_f'&#124; / 2.0) before single-pass VLM extraction.
- **Metrics:** Topic Accuracy (38 classes); Super-category Accuracy (11 groups); Sentiment Accuracy (sentence-embedding cosine >= 0.7); Effectiveness Score (1–5); selected frame count; VLM inference cost (USD)
- **Code url:** Not yet released (abstract states code and evaluation framework will be released upon publication)
- **Code status:** No public repository found as of 2026-10-18.
- **Framework:** Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.1, CLIP ViT-B/32, Whisper-large-v3, Tesseract 5.3, PySceneDetect 0.6 on NVIDIA RTX 4090, plus Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude 3 Haiku APIs.
- **Weights:** Off-the-shelf pretrained models.
- **Features:** 720p resized frames, 512-D CLIP ViT-B/32 embeddings, AlexNet LPIPS activations, Whisper transcripts and RMS/spectral audio features.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary arXiv v1 paper inspected in full; code and the 500-video Pitt Ads evaluation subset manifest are not yet publicly posted.
- **Limitations:** Evaluated on short-form advertisements (mean 38s) using downstream VLM classification accuracy rather than human keyshot overlap F1; 78% of failure cases involve subtle visual/text changes (e.g., 42% subtle text changes, 18% rapid logo transitions) merged by the deduplication cascade. N varies across baselines in Table 2 (251 to 500 videos) due to VLM context-limit failures on high-frame methods like DSNet.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19127v1) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19127v1)

## Audio for Sports Highlight Detection: A Comparative Empirical Study

- **Authors:** Hao Xu; Meenakshi Sarkar; Vishnu Raj; David Gunawan
- **Venue:** MMSports at ACM Multimedia
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17923v1)
- **Project url:** Not independently verified
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** sports highlight detection; multimodal highlight ranking
- **Outputs:** clip saliency; binary highlight regions
- **Mechanisms:** audio-visual feature fusion; temporal GRU; audio source-separation diagnostics
- **Encoders:** Frozen AST audio features and frozen CLIP visual features; MLP and GRU heads compare modalities, while an early projected concatenation feeds the audiovisual GRU.
- **Sampling:** 317 available SV-Highlights videos are divided into non-overlapping 2-second clips; three of the original 320 videos are unavailable.
- **Architecture:** Single-modality MLP/GRU baselines and early-fusion audiovisual GRU; Demucs separates vocal and background tracks for diagnostic experiments.
- **Fusion:** Projected audio and visual embeddings are concatenated before a temporal GRU.
- **Objective:** Binary cross-entropy with AdamW, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 0.0001 and cosine scheduling for 30 epochs.
- **Training data:** SV-Highlights, with labels derived from official edited highlight videos.
- **Test data:** Paper-local held-out SV-Highlights video partitions across three random seeds.
- **Split:** SV-Highlights has no official split. For each seed, videos are divided 80/20 train/test and 20% of training becomes validation (effective 64/16/20); exact IDs are not published.
- **Budget:** No duration budget or summary solver; Hit@K sets K to each video's number of ground-truth positive clips, and temporal IoU thresholds probabilities at 0.5.
- **Postprocessing:** Clip probabilities are ranked for mAP/Hit metrics and thresholded at 0.5 for temporal IoU.
- **Metrics:** mAP; Hit@1; Hit@K; temporal IoU
- **Code url:** Not independently verified
- **Code status:** No author-affiliated repository found through paper, exact-title, arXiv-ID and author searches.
- **Framework:** Paper reports an NVIDIA A100 40 GB and three seeds (42, 2026 and 3020); no dependency manifest or model-selection criterion is published.
- **Weights:** Frozen CLIP, AST and Demucs dependencies; no task checkpoint released.
- **Features:** Paper-local audio, visual and source-separated embeddings; no feature archive or exact split manifest released.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary paper inspected; code, features, split manifests and checkpoints were not available for independent execution.
- **Limitations:** Results use a new paper-local split and cannot be mixed with other SV-Highlights protocols. Three videos are missing, exact split identities and checkpoint selection are unpublished, and editorial highlight videos may omit valid moments. Simple fusion, fixed thresholding and imperfect source separation constrain the conclusions.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.17923v1) · [source 2](https://openreview.net/forum?id=WMHOZw9UdK)

- **Features:** On-the-fly CLIP text/image embeddings and generated visual prototypes; no released feature archive.

- **Limitations:** Metadata availability conditions the task. SumMe uses a video model to infer categories, so it is an auxiliary bootstrapped-metadata protocol rather than the same native-metadata setting as TVSum. Table 2 conflates different dataset-best variants. Sampling, prompt, API, seed and repetition details are incomplete.

## Multimodal Abstractive Summarization of Instructional Videos with Vision-Language Models

- **Authors:** Maham Nazir; Muhammad Aqeel; Richong Zhang; Francesco Setti
- **Venue:** ICPR 2026
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11959v1)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/clipsum)
- **Supervision:** supervised
- **Tasks:** instructional video multimodal abstractive summarization; video-and-transcript-to-text summarization
- **Outputs:** abstractive text summary
- **Mechanisms:** frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 visual encoding; 2-layer temporal Transformer over frame embeddings; mid-layer dimension-adaptive cross-modal attention in BART
- **Encoders:** Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 visual encoder (512-D) and trainable BART-base text encoder-decoder (6 encoder layers, 6 decoder layers, 768-D).
- **Sampling:** M=50 uniformly sampled frames per video resized to 224x224 (25, 50, 100 ablated); procedural step descriptions truncated at 512 BPE tokens.
- **Architecture:** 50 CLIP frame embeddings + learnable positional encodings pass through a 2-layer Transformer (4 heads, FFN 1024), project linearly from 512-D to 768-D, and fuse into BART encoder layer 5 via multi-head cross-modal attention (concatenation + 1536->768 projection + residual + LayerNorm) before encoder layer 6 and 6-layer autoregressive BART decoding.
- **Fusion:** Mid-layer cross-modal attention at BART encoder layer 5 where text representations query projected temporal CLIP visual features (outperforming layer-3 early and layer-6 late fusion).
- **Objective:** Autoregressive token-level negative log-likelihood with teacher forcing; Adam (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, weight decay=1e-5, lr=3e-5 for BART and 1.5e-4 for new layers, batch size 16 x 4 grad accum = 64, up to 100 epochs with early stopping on validation ROUGE-2).
- **Training data:** YouCook2: 1,790 train/validation cooking videos with GPT-3.5-turbo-generated and human-verified abstractive summaries (~24 words, 35% of procedural step length).
- **Test data:** YouCook2 test split (210 videos).
- **Split:** 1,333 train / 457 validation / 210 test videos on YouCook2 (1,790 verified train+val summaries).
- **Budget:** Beam search (beam=5, no-repeat 3-gram blocking) up to 128 tokens (~24 words average target length).
- **Postprocessing:** Evaluated with rouge-score (v0.1.2) for ROUGE-1/2/L F1 and nlg-eval for BLEU-4 precision and METEOR F1.
- **Metrics:** ROUGE-1; ROUGE-2; ROUGE-L; BLEU-4; METEOR
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/clipsum)
- **Code status:** Official repository inspected at commit c3746c1b02b9e6473136f09735e9aa32b1df3e5d (MIT license); contains README documentation only, with source code not yet pushed.
- **Framework:** PyTorch 2.0 on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB).
- **Weights:** Uses pretrained openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 and facebook/bart-base; no trained ClipSum checkpoint uploaded at inspected commit.
- **Features:** 50-frame CLIP ViT-B/32 features and verified GPT-3.5-turbo reference summaries on YouCook2; not yet uploaded to the repository.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary ICPR 2026 / arXiv v1 paper and official GitHub repository at commit c3746c1b02b9e6473136f09735e9aa32b1df3e5d inspected; repository currently hosts only README.md and LICENSE.
- **Limitations:** Reference summaries on YouCook2 were synthesized from procedural step descriptions using GPT-3.5-turbo and manually corrected, rather than authored from scratch by independent human viewers watching the video. Official repository does not yet contain executable code or the verified reference summaries.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11959v1) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.11959v1) · [source 3](https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/clipsum/tree/c3746c1b02b9e6473136f09735e9aa32b1df3e5d)

## Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding

- **Authors:** Shuo Gao; Chenhao Zheng; Zhongzheng Ren
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2026
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16118v1)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://zeld0n.github.io/framepack-U/)
- **Supervision:** training-free; zero-shot
- **Tasks:** constant-memory frame selection and packing for long video understanding; query-guided multi-resolution video compression
- **Outputs:** temporally ordered multi-resolution packed frame sequence; long-video VQA predictions
- **Mechanisms:** CLIP relevance- and diversity-aware greedy frame ranking; hierarchical spatial downsampling under constant O(1) token budget; binary-tree midpoint query-agnostic fallback ordering
- **Encoders:** Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 for query-frame relevance and frame-frame similarity scoring; plugs into off-the-shelf Qwen3.6-27B (dense), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MoE), Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-4B VLMs.
- **Sampling:** Offline all-frame or 1-fps candidate extraction; packs N=346 to 1,664 frames into fixed 128-, 256-, or 512-full-resolution-frame-equivalent token budgets.
- **Architecture:** Two-stage training-free plug-in: (1) greedy selection x_n* = argmax [lambda * CLIP(x_i, q) - (1 - lambda) * max_{x_j in V_tilde} sim(x_i, x_j)] (lambda=0.7) ranks N candidate frames; (2) hierarchical packing assigns spatial downsampling factors d in {1, 2, 4} subject to sum_d (f_d / d^2) <= B and restores chronological order before VLM encoding.
- **Fusion:** Query-frame cosine similarity and visual diversity jointly determine each frame's spatial resolution allocation in the VLM visual token stream.
- **Objective:** Deterministic constrained resolution allocation under constant token budget B (128, 256, or 512 full-frame equivalents) without any model training.
- **Training data:** None; training-free inference method.
- **Test data:** LongVideoBench (LVB), MLVU, and Video-MME (Short/Medium/Long).
- **Split:** Official evaluation splits of LongVideoBench, MLVU and Video-MME.
- **Budget:** Fixed visual token memory budgets equivalent to B in {128, 256, 512} full-resolution frames (e.g., d1f16d2f448 packs 464 frames into 16 + 448/4 = 128 frame equivalents).
- **Postprocessing:** Packed multi-resolution frames are re-sorted into original temporal order and passed to the VLM with standard benchmark prompts.
- **Metrics:** LongVideoBench accuracy; MLVU M-Avg accuracy; Video-MME accuracy; peak GPU memory (GiB); end-to-end latency (s)
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/ZelD0n/framepack-U)
- **Code status:** Official repository inspected at commit aed28d7d61f0a8fa1d601442816ea8c5be48be8b; provides standalone packing scripts, Qwen3-VL monkey-patch integration, and evaluation instructions.
- **Framework:** Python / PyTorch / HuggingFace Transformers / OpenAI CLIP; runtime benchmarked on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU.
- **Weights:** Off-the-shelf CLIP ViT-B/32 and Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 VLM checkpoints.
- **Features:** Pre-extracted or on-the-fly CLIP ViT-B/32 frame embeddings; HuggingFace (`https://huggingface.co/datasets/ZelD0n/FramePack-U`) and ModelScope dataset links provided.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary NeurIPS 2026 / arXiv v1 paper and official repository at commit aed28d7d61f0a8fa1d601442816ea8c5be48be8b inspected; no multi-GPU VLM benchmark run was executed.
- **Limitations:** Adjacent long-video VQA compression method rather than standalone keyshot skim generation. Requires VLMs that process frames independently (less plug-and-play for fixed 3D spatiotemporal grid encoders), and smaller 4B/9B VLMs can suffer slight degradation on MLVU/Video-MME under 512-frame budgets due to reasoning capacity limits.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16118v1) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.16118v1) · [source 3](https://github.com/ZelD0n/framepack-U/tree/aed28d7d61f0a8fa1d601442816ea8c5be48be8b) · [source 4](https://zeld0n.github.io/framepack-U/)

## HAS: Highlight-guided Attention Steering for Multimodal LLM Video Summarization

- **Authors:** Rui Chu; Yingjie Lao
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17994v1)
- **Project url:** Not reported
- **Supervision:** supervised; training-free
- **Tasks:** generic video summarization; cross-modal video-to-video-text summarization; scientific presentation video-to-text summarization
- **Outputs:** frame importance trajectory; text summary; cross-modal V2VT summary
- **Mechanisms:** continuous highlight prior calibration; token-level log-space steering vector; gated inference-time cross-attention head steering
- **Encoders:** Off-the-shelf highlight generator H paired with frozen open-source Video-MLLM backbones: mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave, Video-LLaVA, LLaMA-VID, Video-ChatGPT and Video-LLaMA.
- **Sampling:** Continuous video frame sequence F = [F_1, ..., F_T] with P visual tokens per frame; clip-level raw highlight scores are linearly interpolated to length T and min-max normalized.
- **Architecture:** Lifts calibrated frame-level highlight distribution h in [0,1]^T to token-level steering vector V = log(Repeat(h, P) + epsilon) in R^{TP} and injects row-wise additive logit bias g_{l,m} * beta_{l,m} * V into selected cross-attention heads (l, m) during autoregressive decoding.
- **Fusion:** Prompt-conditioned highlight scores steer text-to-visual cross-attention logits inside the frozen Video-MLLM without hard frame dropping.
- **Objective:** Backbone MLLM and highlight generator remain frozen; lightweight steering gate/strength parameters Theta = {a_{l,m}, beta_{l,m}} are calibrated on a held-out validation set via teacher-forcing NLL plus L1 gate sparsity lambda_s * sum(g_{l,m}).
- **Training data:** Held-out validation/calibration splits of SumMe, TVSum, VideoXum and VISTA for fitting steering policy parameters Theta = {a, beta}; SumMe-trained steering policy is also evaluated zero-shot on a 50-video Mr. HiSum subset.
- **Test data:** SumMe; TVSum; VideoXum; VISTA; 50-video Mr. HiSum subset.
- **Split:** Follows LLMVS on SumMe/TVSum and Mr. HiSum transfer, VideoXum/V2Xum-LLM on VideoXum, and VISTA benchmark splits; exact split manifests and selected highlight generator H are not pinned.
- **Budget:** Continuous full-video token input with soft attention steering; budget-versus-coverage trade-off ablated from 8 to 128 frames/clips on VISTA.
- **Postprocessing:** Autoregressive text generation and temporal salience extraction; evaluated with Kendall tau / Spearman rho on SumMe, TVSum and Mr. HiSum, BLEU-4/METEOR/ROUGE-L/CIDEr/F1/FCLIP/Cross-FCLIP on VideoXum, and RLsum/BERTScore/VideoScore/FactVC on VISTA.
- **Metrics:** Kendall tau; Spearman rho; F1; BLEU-4; METEOR; ROUGE-L; CIDEr; FCLIP; Cross-FCLIP; ROUGE-Lsum; BERTScore; VideoScore; FactVC
- **Code url:** Not reported
- **Code status:** No public repository linked in the paper or found via title/author search.
- **Framework:** PyTorch on NVIDIA L40S GPUs; Adam optimizer for calibrating steering parameters {a, beta}.
- **Weights:** Frozen public checkpoints for mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave, Video-LLaVA, LLaMA-VID, Video-ChatGPT and Video-LLaMA; calibrated steering parameters are not released.
- **Features:** On-the-fly visual tokens and off-the-shelf highlight scores.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary arXiv v1 paper inspected in full; neither the identity of the exact off-the-shelf highlight module H per benchmark nor executable steering code is released.
- **Limitations:** Although described as a training-free backbone plug-in, HAS optimizes per-head gate and strength parameters {a, beta} using teacher-forcing reference-summary NLL on a validation set, and requires an external pretrained highlight detector H whose exact checkpoint and extraction protocol on SumMe/TVSum/VideoXum are not specified.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17994v1) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.17994v1)

- **Reproducibility:** Crossref/OpenAlex/ACM DL bibliographic record and abstract verified (published 2026-10-12); full PDF is closed-access on ACM DL.
- **Limitations:** Abstract-level record only: ACM DL full text is paywalled, so exact LLM backbones, archival corpus provenance (e.g., AAPB/NewsHour) and numerical tables are not independently verified.

## KnowVis: Knowledge-Centric Visual Summarization for Video Lectures

- **Authors:** Yi Xu; Yifan Hou; Xiaoyu Zhang
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint v2; arXiv metadata reports Findings of EMNLP 2026, but an ACL Anthology entry was not independently verified
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03742v2)
- **Project url:** [project url](https://github.com/yixu-cityu/KnowVis)
- **Supervision:** training-free
- **Tasks:** lecture video visual summarization; knowledge-centric educational summarization
- **Outputs:** generated visual summary; knowledge-unit storyboard
- **Mechanisms:** concept graph construction; pedagogical concept selection; retrieval-grounded image generation
- **Encoders:** Proprietary Gemini-3-Flash processes transcripts and slide frames; Gemini-3.1-Flash-Image renders and verifies visual summaries.
- **Sampling:** Transcript chunks and temporally associated slide frames form knowledge units; executable extraction code and exact sampling settings are not released.
- **Architecture:** A prompted pipeline builds a concept graph, selects important/challenging concepts, spreads labels to form knowledge units, generates a storyboard, renders an image and performs one verification pass.
- **Fusion:** Transcript evidence and slide frames are joined through concept-subgraph retrieval rather than learned end-to-end fusion.
- **Objective:** No gradient objective; threshold-concept heuristics and proprietary model prompts drive selection and generation.
- **Training data:** No task-specific model training; 125 open-web lecture videos across ten disciplines are processed into 1,079 knowledge units.
- **Test data:** The same 125-video collection; automated comparison uses generated outputs, and a separate within-subject human study has ten university students.
- **Split:** No train/validation/test partition is reported; the Hugging Face release exposes one knowledge_units split.
- **Budget:** Top 10% important and top 10% challenging concepts seed knowledge-unit construction; no temporal-summary duration budget.
- **Postprocessing:** A generated image receives a single automated verification/revision pass.
- **Metrics:** LLM-judged accuracy; LLM-judged clarity; information density; mental effort; human learning effectiveness; retention; transfer
- **Code url:** [code url](https://github.com/yixu-cityu/KnowVis)
- **Code status:** Official release stub only: the inspected commit contains a README and two images, with no executable implementation.
- **Framework:** Proprietary Gemini APIs; no dependency manifest or runnable source released at the inspected commit.
- **Weights:** Provider-hosted proprietary models; no checkpoints released.
- **Features:** Hugging Face records contain generated images, concepts, concept-subgraph triples, transcripts, slide paths and source-video metadata.
- **Reproducibility:** Paper, Hugging Face schema/listing and repository commit da14209fd4a7483474fad4fefdde8f0920290976 were inspected; the roughly 803 MB dataset and proprietary pipeline were not downloaded or run.
- **Limitations:** Proprietary model versions, prompts and provider behavior limit repeatability. Automated judges may favor related model families; failed baseline generations change denominators. The human study has ten participants. The live dataset card does not declare the license stated prospectively in the paper.
- **Verified on:** 2026-09-19
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.03742v2) · [source 2](https://github.com/yixu-cityu/KnowVis/tree/da14209fd4a7483474fad4fefdde8f0920290976) · [source 3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yixu-cityu/KnowVis/tree/ba4208a250bc60b03d0b4ea48f1c2dc70c2d77cc)

## LVSum: A Benchmark for Timestamp-Aware Long Video Summarization

- **Authors:** Alkesh Patel; Melis Ozyildirim; Ying-Chang Cheng; Ganesh Nagarajan
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (v2)
- **Year:** 2026
- **Paper url:** [paper url](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10024v2)
- **Project url:** Not independently verified
- **Supervision:** training-free; zero-shot
- **Tasks:** timestamp-aware long-video summarization; video-to-video-text (V2VT) summarization benchmarking
- **Outputs:** timestamped video intervals; interval importance scores (1–3); segment text descriptions
- **Mechanisms:** multimodal LLM long-video prompting; 1-fps second-level rank correlation evaluation; MLLM-as-Judge Content Relevance (CR) and Modality Coherence (MC)
- **Encoders:** Evaluates Claude Opus-4.5 (and Sonnet-4.5), Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct; Gemini-2.5-Pro generates timestamped ASR transcripts and serves as the CR/MC judge.
- **Sampling:** 96 uniformly sampled video frames (24, 32, 64, 96, 128 ablated) paired with timestamped transcripts; importance rankings are evaluated at 1-fps (second-level) granularity.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark and evaluation protocol prompting MLLMs to output a list of HH:MM:SS - HH:MM:SS segments, 0–3 relevance scores, and concise descriptions under a <=15% total duration constraint.
- **Fusion:** Interleaved sampled video frames with timestamp lists and full transcripts in the MLLM context window; paper diagnoses 'modality interference' and 'instruction drift' in Qwen3-VL-235B when combining video and transcript.
- **Objective:** Zero-shot instruction following under a 15% duration budget; evaluated via 1-fps Kendall tau / Spearman rho and 1–5 Likert MLLM-as-Judge Content Relevance (CR) and Modality Coherence (MC).
- **Training data:** None; evaluation-only benchmark.
- **Test data:** LVSum: 72 English videos (10–55 minutes, mean 16 minutes) across 13 categories with 10 independent human annotations per video.
- **Split:** 72 evaluation videos (filtered from 100 sampled out of ~4,000 crawled web videos); human upper bound uses leave-one-out across the 10 annotators.
- **Budget:** 15% maximum summary duration constraint specified in annotator guidelines and model prompts (human average ~10%; Gemini-2.5-Pro ~12%; Opus-4.5 ~30%; Qwen3-VL-235B ~56%).
- **Postprocessing:** Predicted segment scores are mapped to a 1-fps timeline for tau/rho; Section 5.2 also evaluates hard length-constrained truncation retaining highest-ranked segments up to 10–30% budgets.
- **Metrics:** Kendall tau; Spearman rho; Content Relevance (CR); Modality Coherence (MC); summary length ratio
- **Code url:** Not yet released (paper footnote 1 states dataset and code will be released upon acceptance)
- **Code status:** No public repository or dataset archive found as of 2026-10-18; full prompts and guidelines are published in Appendices A–D.
- **Framework:** Proprietary APIs (Opus-4.5, Gemini-2.5-Pro) and open-weight Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct.
- **Weights:** Off-the-shelf foundation models.
- **Features:** 96 uniformly sampled frames and Gemini-2.5-Pro timestamped transcripts.
- **Reproducibility:** Primary arXiv v2 paper (including full annotation guidelines and summarization/judge prompts in Appendices A–D) inspected; dataset and code are not yet publicly posted.
- **Limitations:** Dataset and code are pending publication release. MLLM-as-Judge (Gemini-2.5-Pro) may exhibit self-preference when scoring Gemini-2.5-Pro outputs (which achieve the highest CR=3.28 and MC=4.32). Text in Section 4.1 names Sonnet-4.5 while all tables and discussion report Opus-4.5.
- **Verified on:** 2026-10-18
- **Sources:** [source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10024v2) · [source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.10024v2)
